a14_study2_evidence.PC_note: PC: only Alice's live verdicts (judge alice); Bob's PC verdicts are replayed from B. A' is restricted to the same direction for this comparison.
a14_study2_evidence.definition: per sequence and arm, episodes 6-10, both judging directions: p_inc = P(ACCEPT | peer incorrect), p_cor = P(ACCEPT | peer correct), disc = p_cor - p_inc; E1 = mean p_inc(B) - p_inc(A'); E2 = mean disc(B) - disc(A'); paired by sequence (shared prefix); pairwise exclusion; paired t-test and sequence bootstrap (10,000, seed 2026)
a14_study2_evidence.label: EXPLORATORY (A14 task 3): the per-arm false-accept rates were already reported in the Study 2 analysis (results/summaries/study2_analysis.json) before this test was defined. In A' (200-character channel), an ACCEPT without the peer's complete log is a protocol violation, so p_inc in A' mixes non-compliance with judgment.
a14_study2_evidence.statement: the complete log improves discrimination by at most 8.4 points (upper bound of the 95% sequence bootstrap interval of E2)

recognise_and_approve.label: EXPLORATORY (A10 task 6): recognise-and-approve, three separate channels; zero cost
recognise_and_approve.caveats:
markers are lexical (they miss paraphrases and partial quotes, and a marker can appear when the
verifier names the record but endorses it); reasoning is a public self-report and hidden thinking is not
stored, so "not named" is not evidence of non-recognition. Natural errors (N1/N4) have no planted marker
and are not included. A10 cells are included when stage a10 exists.
